title: Climate Change Explained
summary: The greenhouse effect, what changes the climate and what people can do.

steps.title: The blanket around Earth
sentences: Some gases in the air, like carbon dioxide and methane, act like a blanket that traps the Sun's heat.
This is the greenhouse effect, and a natural amount of it keeps Earth warm enough for life.
Without it Earth would be an icy planet.
points: A little is needed for life

steps.title: Too much blanket
sentences: When we burn coal, oil and gas for power, vehicles and factories, extra carbon dioxide goes into the air.
Cutting down forests also adds carbon dioxide and removes trees that absorb it.
The extra gas traps more heat, so the planet's average temperature is rising.

steps.title: What changes
sentences: Scientists see ice melting, sea levels rising and more extreme weather such as heatwaves and heavy rain.
Coastal cities like Chennai face higher risks from rising seas and strong storms.
The pace and size of the changes depend on what the world does next.

steps.title: What we can do
sentences: We can use less energy, switch to solar and wind power, plant trees and waste less food.
Walking, cycling or using public transport instead of cars helps.
Small choices add up when millions of people make them.

facts: Global average temperature has risen by about 1.1 to 1.2 degrees Celsius since the late 1800s.
India is investing a lot in solar power and has one of the world's largest solar programmes.
Trees take in carbon dioxide as they grow.

quiz.q: Which gas is a main greenhouse gas?
quiz.why: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere.

quiz.q: Why do coastal cities worry about climate change?
quiz.why: Higher seas and stronger storms threaten coasts.

notes: Temperature figures come from major scientific assessments (for example the IPCC) and are updated every few years.
